issues.legal_issue: A tenant who is wrongfully dispossessed remains a tenant, and may retain a preferential right to pre-empt a sale, unless the tenancy is lawfully terminated.
material_facts: The lower courts found that the plaintiff was a tenant of the land on the date it was sold.
The vendees forcibly dispossessed the tenant after the sale.
The tenant’s tenancy was not shown to have been terminated on a ground authorized by the applicable tenancy law.
The tenant applied to the revenue authority for restoration of possession.
issues.conclusion: The tenant was deemed to remain a tenant on the sale date and the other material dates, and was entitled to pre-empt the land.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 4, 7 and 7A of the Pepsu Tenancy and Agricultural Lands Act, 1955, override inconsistent laws and require a lawful ground and an order or decree for eviction to determine a tenancy. Applying Rikki Ram v. Ram Kumar, the Court held that a person with a right to possess land remains its tenant despite wrongful dispossession, particularly where proceedings to recover possession have been initiated. The tenant must have a subsisting pre-emption right on the material dates, as referred to in Bhagwan Das v. Chet Ram; Dindyal v. Rajaram was also cited. The Court confined its conclusion to the provisions before it.

rule.if: preemption_suit and tenant_on_sale_date and wrongfully_dispossessed and not tenancy_lawfully_terminated and restoration_proceedings_started

predicates.preemption_suit: The proceeding is a claim to pre-empt a sale of land.
predicates.tenant_on_sale_date: The claimant was a tenant of the land when it was sold.
predicates.wrongfully_dispossessed: The claimant was put out of possession without lawful authority.
predicates.tenancy_lawfully_terminated: The tenancy was terminated on a lawful ground through the required process.
predicates.restoration_proceedings_started: The claimant initiated proceedings to recover possession of the land.
predicates.tenant_remains_eligible_to_preempt: The claimant remains a tenant entitled to exercise the preferential right to pre-empt the sale.

issues.definition: When a tenant in a pre-emption suit was a tenant on the sale date, was wrongfully dispossessed, has not had the tenancy lawfully terminated, and has begun recovery proceedings, the tenant remains eligible to pre-empt.

issues.legal_issue: A contention not raised in the pleadings or in the appeals before the lower courts cannot be advanced for the first time in the further appeal in the circumstances of this case.
material_facts: The appellants argued that the tenant’s failure to sue for recovery of possession within the prescribed period had extinguished his right and title.
That contention had not been raised in the appellants’ written statement or in the grounds of their appeals before the lower courts.
issues.conclusion: The appellants could not canvass that contention for the first time in the further appeal.
issues.legal_principle: The Court declined to entertain the contention because it had not been raised in the pleadings or in the grounds of appeal before the lower courts.

predicates.further_appeal: The proceeding is a further appeal from decisions of lower courts.
predicates.contention_not_raised_in_pleadings_or_lo: The party did not raise the contention in its pleadings or in its appeals before the lower courts.
predicates.new_contention_not_entertained: The party is not permitted to advance the contention for the first time in the further appeal.

issues.definition: In a further appeal, a contention omitted from the pleadings and the appeals before the lower courts is not entertained.
